title.en: Trajan Launched the First Dacian War

summary.en: In AD 101, Roman Emperor Trajan led his forces across the newly built stone bridge over the Danube, launching the First Dacian War. Trajan's army defeated the forces of the Dacian king Decebalus on the Danube. The war continued until AD 102, when Dacia was forced to accept Roman peace terms.

statement.en:
In AD 101, Roman Emperor Trajan led his forces across the newly built stone bridge over the Danube, launching the First Dacian War. Trajan's army defeated the forces of the Dacian king Decebalus on the Danube. The war continued until AD 102, when Dacia was forced to accept Roman peace terms.

title.en: Ban Chao, Protector General of the Western Regions, returns to Luoyang and dies of illness

summary.en: After 31 years in the Western Regions, Ban Chao, old and ill, petitioned to retire to his hometown. Emperor He of Han granted permission. His sister Ban Zhao personally greeted him at the city gate; the siblings wept with emotion. Only a month after returning to Luoyang, Ban Chao died of old war wounds and travel fatigue at age 71. The court posthumously honored him and bestowe

statement.zh: 在西域经营31年的班超因年老体衰上书请求告老还乡，汉和帝准其返回洛阳。其妹班昭亲自到城门迎接，兄妹相见涕泪交流。班超回京后仅一个月便因旧伤复发和长途劳累去世，享年71岁。朝廷追赠其为西域都护、谥号定远侯，并派遣使者吊唁。班超以“不入虎穴，焉得虎子”的勇气收复西域，保障丝路畅通三十余年，其功绩成为东汉外交史上最辉煌的一页。
statement.en:
After 31 years in the Western Regions, Ban Chao, old and ill, petitioned to retire to his hometown. Emperor He of Han granted permission. His sister Ban Zhao personally greeted him at the city gate; the siblings wept with emotion. Only a month after returning to Luoyang, Ban Chao died of old war wounds and travel fatigue at age 71. The court posthumously honored him and bestowed the title Marquis Dingyuan. Ban Chao’s courage ('How can one catch tiger cubs without entering the tiger's lair?') in recovering the Western Regions and ensuring Silk Road peace for more than three decades became the most brilliant chapter in Eastern Han diplomacy.

statement.zh: 在罗马帝国统治下，埃及亚历山大图书馆成为当时地中海世界的学术中心。本年图书馆举办了关于“宇宙中心是地心还是日心”的公开辩论，来自希腊、犹太、埃及的学者们运用数学与哲学工具激烈交锋。虽然最终地心说占上风，但辩论促使托勒密等学者进一步观测天文数据。此次活动还整理了馆藏70万卷纸莎草文献，吸引了大量学者在此从事数学、医学和天文学研究，延续了托勒密王朝时代的学术繁荣。
statement.en:
Under Roman rule, the Library of Alexandria remained the Mediterranean's leading academic center. That year, a public debate was held on whether the universe was geocentric or heliocentric. Scholars from Greek, Jewish, and Egyptian backgrounds clashed vigorously using mathematics and philosophy. Although the geocentric view won, the debate prompted scholars like Ptolemy to further observe astronomical data. The event also organized the library's 700,000 papyrus scrolls, attracting many scholars to study mathematics, medicine, and astronomy, continuing the scholarly prosperity from the Ptolemaic era.

title.en: Construction begins on Trajan's Forum in Rome

summary.en: Using the enormous spoils from the Dacian Wars, Emperor Trajan initiated a grand architectural complex in Rome – Trajan's Forum. Measuring 300 meters long and 185 meters wide, it was four times larger than the earlier Forum of Augustus. statement.zh: 罗马皇帝图拉真用征服达契亚获得的巨额战利品，在罗马城中心启动了一个宏伟的建筑群——图拉真广场。广场长300米、宽185米，比之前的奥古斯都广场大四倍。中央矗立着图拉真骑马镀金铜像，后方是高达38米的图拉真纪功柱，柱身螺旋浮雕长达200米。刻画了两次达契亚战争的155个场景。广场两侧设有两个对称的图书馆（希腊文馆和拉丁文馆）以及巨大的市场大厅。整个工程使用了数万吨卡拉拉大理石，雇佣了上万名工匠和奴隶，历时五年完工，成为古代世界最壮观的公共建筑群之一。象征罗马帝国的强盛与图拉真的武功。
statement.en: Using the enormous spoils from the Dacian Wars, Emperor Trajan initiated a grand architectural complex in Rome – Trajan's Forum. Measuring 300 meters long and 185 meters wide, it was four times larger than the earlier Forum of Augustus. At its center stood a gilded equestrian statue of Trajan; behind it rose the 38-meter-high Trajan's Column, its spiral relief 200 meters long depicting 155 scenes from the Dacian Wars. On either side were two symmetrical libraries (Greek and Latin) and a large market hall. The project consumed 10,000 of tons of Carrara marble, employed over 10,000 craftsmen and slaves, and took five years to complete, becoming one of the most magnificent public complexes of the ancient world, symbolizing Roman power and Trajan's martial glory.

At its center stood a gilded equestrian statue of Trajan; behind it rose the 38-meter-high Trajan's Column, its spiral relief 200 meters long depicting 155 scenes from the Dacian Wars. title.en: Emperor He of Han tours Jingzhou to inspect water conservancy projects

summary.en: Emperor He, accompanied by Empress Deng Sui and officials, toured Jingzhou, focusing on the embankment and irrigation works along the Yangtze and Han Rivers. Jingzhou had suffered frequent floods; the court had allocated 5 million coins to build a 300-li long flood control dike and dredge numerous canals. The emperor personally ascended the dike, offered wine and meat to the la

statement.zh: 汉和帝刘肇携带皇后邓绥及文武百官南巡荆州，重点视察了长江、汉水沿岸的水利堤防工程。此前荆州水患频繁，朝廷拨款五百万钱兴修了长达三百里的防洪堤坝，并疏浚了多条灌溉渠道。和帝亲自登上堤坝询问工程进展，赐修堤民夫酒肉。南巡期间他还召见当地耆老，免除荆州全年赋税，并选拔了二十名孝廉入太学。此次南巡缓和了朝廷与地方矛盾，促进了南方经济发展。
statement.en:
Emperor He, accompanied by Empress Deng Sui and officials, toured Jingzhou, focusing on the embankment and irrigation works along the Yangtze and Han Rivers. Jingzhou had suffered frequent floods; the court had allocated 5 million coins to build a 300-li long flood control dike and dredge numerous canals. The emperor personally ascended the dike, offered wine and meat to the laborers, exempted Jingzhou from all taxes for the year, and selected twenty filial and incorrupt candidates for the Imperial University. title.en: Emperor He of Han dies; a hundred-day-old infant ascends as Emperor Shang

summary.en: In winter of the 17th year of Yongyuan (105), 27-year-old Emperor He of Han died in Luoyang's Southern Palace, possibly from chronic mercury poisoning from alchemical elixirs. His only son, Liu Long, just a hundred days old, was enthroned as Emperor Shang under the regency of Empress Dowager Deng. She assumed power and appointed her brother Deng Zhi as General of Chariots and C

statement.zh: 东汉永元17年（105）冬，年仅27岁的汉和帝刘肇在洛阳南宫驾崩，死因可能是长期服食丹药导致慢性中毒。和帝仅有一子刘隆出生刚满一百日，在邓皇后（后为邓太后）的主持下被立为皇帝，是为汉殇帝。邓太后临朝称制，以兄长邓骘为车骑将军辅政。殇帝年幼，朝政大权完全落入邓氏外戚手中，开启了东汉外戚长期专权的局面。
statement.en:
In winter of the 17th year of Yongyuan (105), 27-year-old Emperor He of Han died in Luoyang's Southern Palace, possibly from chronic mercury poisoning from alchemical elixirs. His only son, Liu Long, just a hundred days old, was enthroned as Emperor Shang under the regency of Empress Dowager Deng. She assumed power and appointed her brother Deng Zhi as General of Chariots and Cavalry. With the infant emperor, court power fell completely into the hands of the Deng clan, beginning an era of prolonged eunuch and consort clan domination.

For Asia in 105 CE, “Emperor He of Han dies; a hundred-day-old infant ascends as Emperor Shang” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Trajan launches the Second Dacian War

summary.en: Decebalus, king of Dacia, despite submitting after the First Dacian War, again violated the treaty, expanded his army, and raided Roman borders. statement.zh: 达契亚国王德凯巴鲁斯在第一次战争后虽被迫臣服，但再次违反和约、扩军备战并袭击罗马边境。罗马皇帝图拉真亲率大军渡过多瑙河，采用分进合击战术深入达契亚腹地。经过激烈战斗，罗马军队攻陷达契亚首都萨尔米泽杰图萨，德凯巴鲁斯逃入山区组织游击战。此战为罗马彻底征服达契亚奠定了基础，掠夺的巨额黄金使罗马财政充盈，为后续大规模公共建筑提供了资金。
statement.en:
Decebalus, king of Dacia, despite submitting after the First Dacian War, again violated the treaty, expanded his army, and raided Roman borders. Emperor Trajan of Rome personally led a large army across the Danube, employing a pincer movement deep into Dacian territory. After fierce fighting, the Romans captured the Dacian capital Sarmizegetusa Regia. Decebalus fled to the mountains to wage guerrilla warfare. This battle laid the foundation for Rome's total conquest of Dacia, and the immense gold looted filled Rome's treasury, funding subsequent large-scale public construction.

For Europe in 105 CE, “Trajan launches the Second Dacian War” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Deng Zhi appointed Grand General as regent

summary.en: To consolidate consort clan power, Empress Dowager Deng promoted her brother Deng Zhi to Grand General, ranking above the Three Excellences, commanding all military forces. Though from a consort clan, Deng Zhi was modest, humble, and a Confucian scholar. He recommended talents like Yang Zhen and Chen Chan, and advocated tax reduction and disaster relief. However, the Grand Gene

statement.zh: 邓太后为了巩固外戚专权，提拔其兄长邓骘为大将军，位在三公之上，掌全国兵权。邓骘虽出身外戚，但为人恭谨谦逊、崇尚儒学，上任后推荐了杨震、陈禅等贤才，并建议减免赋税、赈济灾民。然而，大将军府权倾朝野，各地奏章必须先送大将军府审核，才能呈报皇帝，这加剧了东汉外戚专政的政治危机。
statement.en:
To consolidate consort clan power, Empress Dowager Deng promoted her brother Deng Zhi to Grand General, ranking above the Three Excellences, commanding all military forces. Though from a consort clan, Deng Zhi was modest, humble, and a Confucian scholar. He recommended talents like Yang Zhen and Chen Chan, and advocated tax reduction and disaster relief. However, the Grand General's office wielded immense power; all reports had to be reviewed there before reaching the emperor, worsening the political crisis of consort clan domination.

For Asia in 107 CE, “Deng Zhi appointed Grand General as regent” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Tacitus writes his Histories

With incisive prose

statement.zh: 罗马最伟大的历史学家普布利乌斯·科尔奈利乌斯·塔西佗开始撰写其代表作《历史》。该书共十二卷（仅前五卷和部分残篇传世），详细记述了公元69-96年罗马帝国的历史，包括四帝内乱、韦帕芗建立弗拉维王朝和图密善的暴政。塔西佗以犀利的文笔和深刻的政治洞察，揭露了专制制度下人性的扭曲和道德的堕落。其另一部著作《编年史》涵盖提比略到尼禄时期，共同构成了早期罗马帝国最宝贵的史料来源。
statement.en:
The greatest Roman historian, Publius Cornelius Tacitus, began writing his magnum opus, the Histories. The work, originally 12 books (only the first five and fragments survive), details the history of the Roman Empire from AD 69 to 96, including the Year of the Four Emperors, the founding of the Flavian dynasty by Vespasian, and the tyranny of Domitian. With incisive prose and profound political insight, Tacitus exposed the distortion of human nature and moral decay under autocracy. His other major work, the Annals, covers the period from Tiberius to Nero, together forming the most invaluable historical source for the early Roman Empire.

For Europe in 108 CE, “Tacitus writes his Histories” is a traceable node of Culture change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Border conflict erupts between Goguryeo and Eastern Han

summary.en: Taking advantage of the Han's preoccupation with the Qiang rebellion, King Goguryeo (Taejo) led an invasion of the Han commanderies of Liaodong and Xuantu, plundering people and livestock. statement.zh: 高句丽太祖王高宫趁东汉忙于镇压羌人起义之机，率军入侵东汉辽东郡和玄菟郡，掠夺人口和牲畜。辽东太守蔡讽率军迎战，兵败战死，数千汉军被歼。汉安帝震怒，下令玄菟郡和辽东属国集结兵马反击，击败高句丽军，收复失地，并斩杀高句丽将领数人。高宫被迫求和，送还掠走的汉朝百姓，向汉朝进贡貂皮、好马以示臣服。此后数十年，高句丽表面顺服，暗中仍不断扩张势力。
statement.en:
Taking advantage of the Han's preoccupation with the Qiang rebellion, King Goguryeo (Taejo) led an invasion of the Han commanderies of Liaodong and Xuantu, plundering people and livestock. Liaodong governor Cai Fan led his forces to meet them but was defeated and killed, with thousands of Han soldiers lost. Emperor An was enraged and ordered a counterattack by troops from Xuantu and the Liaodong Dependent State. They defeated the Goguryeo army, recovering lost territory and killing several Goguryeo generals. Goguryeo was forced to sue for peace, returning the kidnapped Han civilians and offering tribute of sable furs and fine horses as tokens of submission. For decades afterward, Goguryeo outwardly complied while secretly expanding its power.

title.en: Pliny the Younger publishes his Letters

summary.en: Roman author and senator Pliny the Younger compiled his personal correspondence with friends, emperors, and scholars over many years into nine volumes. The letters cover a wide range of topics: daily life, literary criticism, courtroom advocacy, social customs, and political events. Most famous are his two letters to the historian Tacitus, giving a detailed account of the erupt

statement.zh: 罗马作家、元老院议员小普林尼将多年来与朋友、皇帝和学者之间的私人通信整理成9卷出版。这些书信内容丰富，涉及日常生活、文学鉴赏、法庭辩护、社会风俗和政治事件。其中最著名的是他写给历史学家塔西佗的两封信，详细描述了公元79年维苏威火山爆发的情景及其叔父老普林尼遇难的经过。这些信件是第一手历史资料，生动再现了罗马帝国的社会风貌，成为研究罗马历史的珍贵文献。
statement.en:
Roman author and senator Pliny the Younger compiled his personal correspondence with friends, emperors, and scholars over many years into 9 volumes. The letters cover a wide range of topics: daily life, literary criticism, courtroom advocacy, social customs, and political events. Most famous are his two letters to the historian Tacitus, giving a detailed account of the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in AD 79 and the death of his uncle, Pliny the Elder. These firsthand accounts vividly portray Roman society and are invaluable historical documents.

For Europe in 109 CE, “Pliny the Younger publishes his Letters” is a traceable node of Culture change whose significance is best read through later events.

statement.zh: 图拉真占领美索不达米亚后，帕提亚帝国各地纷纷爆发反抗罗马占领的武装起义。帕提亚王室成员和贵族领袖趁罗马主力北调之际，在巴比伦尼亚、苏萨等地组织抵抗运动。起义军采用游击战术，袭击罗马补给线和孤立哨所，致使罗马军队陷入治安战的泥潭。图拉真被迫从波斯湾回师镇压，但无法彻底肃清抵抗力量。帕提亚人民的顽强抵抗最终迫使继任皇帝哈德良放弃美索不达米亚。
statement.en:
After Trajan's occupation of Mesopotamia, anti-Roman resistance erupted throughout the Parthian Empire. Parthian royals and nobles organized guerrilla warfare in Babylonia, Susa, and elsewhere, attacking Roman supply lines and isolated outposts while the main Roman forces were deployed north. Trajan was forced to march back from the Persian Gulf to suppress them, but could not eliminate all resistance. The tenacious Parthian resistance ultimately forced Hadrian, Trajan's successor, to abandon Mesopotamia.

title.en: Eastern Han relocates people from frontier commanderies of Liangzhou to the interior

summary.en: Under pressure from the ongoing Qiang rebellion, the Han court ordered the forced relocation of people from border commanderies such as Longxi, Anding, Beidi, and Shangjun to the interior (Guanzhong, Hedong, etc.). Troops were sent to drive away reluctant residents, burning their houses and crops. Hundreds of thousands became homeless, and many died of cold, hunger, or Qiang at

statement.zh: 面对羌人起义的持续压力，东汉朝廷下诏将凉州陇西、安定、北地、上郡等边境郡县的百姓强制迁往关中、河东等内地。朝廷派军队驱赶不愿离开的百姓，烧毁其房屋和庄稼，造成数十万人流离失所，大量百姓在迁徙途中冻饿而死或遭羌军劫杀。这种“弃边保内”的政策虽然短期内减少了边境防御压力，但导致大片国土沦陷，边境经济崩溃，东汉政权声望严重受损。
statement.en:
Under pressure from the ongoing Qiang rebellion, the Han court ordered the forced relocation of people from border commanderies such as Longxi, Anding, Beidi, and Shangjun to the interior (Guanzhong, Hedong, etc.). Troops were sent to drive away reluctant residents, burning their houses and crops. 100,000 became homeless, and many died of cold, hunger, or Qiang attacks during the migration. This 'abandon the border, protect the interior' policy reduced short-term border pressure, but led to the loss of vast territories, the collapse of border economies, and severe damage to the Han court's prestige.

For Asia in 111 CE, “Eastern Han relocates people from frontier commanderies of Liangzhou to the interior” is a traceable node of Society change whose significance is best read through later events.

zh: 面对羌人起义的持续压力，东汉朝廷下诏将凉州陇西、安定、北地、上郡等边境郡县的百姓强制迁往关中、河东等内地。朝廷派军队驱赶不愿离开的百姓，烧毁其房屋和庄稼，造成数十万人流离失所，大量百姓在迁徙途中冻饿而死或遭羌军劫杀。这种“弃边保内”的政策虽然短期内减少了边境防御压力，但导致大片国土沦陷，边境经济崩溃，东汉政权声望严重受损。
面对羌人起义的持续压力，东汉朝廷下诏将凉州陇西、安定、北地、上郡等边境郡县的百姓强制迁往关中、河东等内地。
en: Under pressure from the ongoing Qiang rebellion, the Han court ordered the forced relocation of people from border commanderies such as Longxi, Anding, Beidi, and Shangjun to the interior (Guanzhong, Hedong, etc.). Troops were sent to drive away reluctant residents, burning their houses and crops. 100,000 became homeless, and many died of cold, hunger, or Qiang attacks during the migration. This 'abandon the border, protect the interior' policy reduced short-term border pressure, but led to the loss of vast territories, the collapse of border economies, and severe damage to the Han court's prestige.

title.en: Inauguration of Trajan's Column

summary.en: Emperor Trajan held a grand inauguration ceremony for Trajan's Column in his forum, commemorating his victory in the Dacian Wars. The column stands about 38 meters tall, built from 20 massive blocks of Carrara marble, with an internal spiral staircase of 185 steps leading to the top. The column's shaft is wrapped in a 200-meter-long spiral frieze depicting scenes from the wars:

statement.zh: 罗马皇帝图拉真为纪念达契亚战争的胜利，在图拉真广场举行盛大的纪功柱落成典礼。纪功柱高约38米，由20块巨型卡拉拉大理石堆叠而成，内部有185级螺旋楼梯通向柱顶。柱身环绕着长达200米的浮雕带，刻画了战争场景：罗马军队渡过多瑙河、围攻敌城、处决战俘等155个场景。共出现约2600个人物。柱顶原本立有图拉真雕像（16世纪被换成圣彼得雕像）。纪功柱是罗马艺术与工程学的杰作，也是后世纪念性建筑的范本。

title.en: The Maoling and Huo Qubing's tomb

summary.en: Emperor Wu's Maoling and the attached tomb of General Huo Qubing were built at Xingping, Shaanxi; Huo's 'horse trampling the Xiongnu' relief is a masterpiece of early Chinese funerary sculpture.

statement.zh:
汉武帝茂陵及其陪葬的霍去病墓在陕西兴平营建，霍墓“马踏匈奴”石雕是中国早期陵墓石刻杰作。陵区以封土、陪葬墓与石雕组成纪念空间，石雕借体量与题材宣示军功；陵墓制度体现皇权与功臣秩序。石刻成为汉代艺术的代表。

把「茂陵与霍去病墓」放回公元113年的汉，可以看到建筑变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Eastern Han court issues decree to rectify public finances

summary.en: Due to years of costly war against the Qiang, the Eastern Han faced a severe fiscal deficit. Empress Dowager Deng's court ordered a nationwide rectification of finances. The decree required every commandery and county to strictly audit household registrations and farmland, crack down on powerful families hiding population and evading taxes; abolish redundant officials, reduce p

statement.zh: 由于连年对羌战争耗费巨资，东汉财政严重赤字，邓太后朝廷下令在全国范围内整顿财政。法令要求各郡县严格核查户籍和田亩，打击豪强隐瞒人口、逃避赋税的行为；裁撤冗余官员，削减皇室开支；同时规定地方官员不得再向百姓征收“巧立名目”的杂税。整顿虽在一定程度上增加了财政收入，但触动豪强利益，遭到抵制，执行效果有限。
statement.en:
Due to years of costly war against the Qiang, the Eastern Han faced a severe fiscal deficit. Empress Dowager Deng's court ordered a nationwide rectification of finances. The decree required every commandery and county to strictly audit household registrations and farmland, crack down on powerful families hiding population and evading taxes; abolish redundant officials, reduce palace expenditures; and forbid local officials from levying miscellaneous taxes under false pretexts. Though the rectification somewhat increased revenue, it sparked resistance from powerful interests and had limited effect.

For Asia in 113 CE, “Eastern Han court issues decree to rectify public finances” is a traceable node of Economy change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Emperor An of Han changes era name to Yuanchu

summary.en: Praying for peace and stability and to end the Qiang rebellion, Emperor An decreed a change of era name to 'Yuanchu' (Primary Beginning). The change included a general amnesty (except for heinous crimes), a reduction of one degree in punishments for prisoners, and an order for local authorities to recommend 'filial and incorrupt' and 'flourishing talent' candidates for office,

statement.zh: 汉安帝刘祜为祈求国泰民安、平息羌乱，下令改年号为“元初”。改元大赦天下，除十恶不赦之外，囚犯一律减刑一等。同时下令各地举荐“孝廉”和“茂才”入朝为官，并免除贫苦百姓拖欠的赋税。但改元并未改变东汉内外交困的局面，羌人起义仍在继续，国库依旧空虚。
statement.en:
Praying for peace and stability and to end the Qiang rebellion, Emperor An decreed a change of era name to 'Yuanchu' (Primary Beginning). The change included a general amnesty (except for heinous crimes), a reduction of one degree in punishments for prisoners, and an order for local authorities to recommend 'filial and incorrupt' and 'flourishing talent' candidates for office, while also forgiving back taxes owed by the poor. However, the era change did little to change the Eastern Han's internal and external difficulties: the Qiang revolt continued, and the treasury remained empty.

For Asia in 114 CE, “Emperor An of Han changes era name to Yuanchu” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Hadrian succeeds as Roman emperor

summary.en: Emperor Trajan died of illness during his Parthian campaign at Selinus in Asia Minor. On his deathbed, he adopted his cousin Hadrian as his son and designated him successor. Hadrian, then serving as governor of Syria in Antioch, quickly returned to Rome, where the Senate, under pressure from the army, recognized him as emperor. Hadrian immediately reversed Trajan's expansionist

statement.zh: 罗马皇帝图拉真在远征帕提亚途中病逝于小亚细亚的塞利努斯，临终前他收养表弟哈德良为养子并指定为继承人。哈德良当时正在安条克担任叙利亚总督，得到消息后迅速返回罗马，元老院迫于军队压力承认其为皇帝。哈德良即位后立即改变图拉真的扩张政策，放弃美索不达米亚等难以防守的东方领土，采取防御战略，修建长城巩固边境。
statement.en:
Emperor Trajan died of illness during his Parthian campaign at Selinus in Asia Minor. On his deathbed, he adopted his cousin Hadrian as his son and designated him successor. Hadrian, then serving as governor of Syria in Antioch, quickly returned to Rome, where the Senate, under pressure from the army, recognized him as emperor. Hadrian immediately reversed Trajan's expansionist policy, abandoning hard-to-defend eastern territories like Mesopotamia and adopting a defensive strategy, building walls to strengthen the borders.

title.en: Roman Emperor Hadrian abandons Mesopotamia

summary.en: New Emperor Hadrian considered Trajan's conquests in Mesopotamia difficult and costly to defend, especially given ongoing Parthian uprisings. statement.zh: 新任罗马皇帝哈德良认为图拉真征服的美索不达米亚地区难以防守且耗费巨大，加之当地帕提亚人不断起义，于是下令罗马军队撤出美索不达米亚，退回幼发拉底河以西。哈德良与帕提亚国王缔结和约，承认帕提亚对两河流域的主权，亚美尼亚则成为罗马和帕提亚的缓冲国。此举虽然遭到主战派元老的批评，但有效收缩了防线，使罗马集中兵力应对欧洲边境的蛮族威胁。
statement.en:
New Emperor Hadrian considered Trajan's conquests in Mesopotamia difficult and costly to defend, especially given ongoing Parthian uprisings. He therefore ordered a Roman withdrawal from Mesopotamia back to the west bank of the Euphrates. Hadrian made peace with the Parthian king, recognizing Parthian sovereignty over Mesopotamia, while Armenia became a buffer state between Rome and Parthia. Though criticized by pro-war senators, the move effectively shortened Rome's defensive lines, allowing concentration of forces against barbarian threats in Europe.

title.en: Construction of Hadrian's Wall officially begins

summary.en: Emperor Hadrian personally presided over the foundation ceremony of Hadrian's Wall. statement.zh: 罗马皇帝哈德良亲自主持哈德良长城的奠基仪式。长城东起泰恩河口，西至索尔韦湾，全长约117公里。墙体使用石料和草泥砖，高约4.5米，宽2.5-3米，每隔一罗马里建有一座里堡，两座里堡间设两座瞭望塔。长城北侧挖掘深约3米的壕沟。工程动用了三个军团约一万五千名士兵，耗时六年完工。哈德良长城成为罗马帝国最坚固的北方防线，有效遏制了皮克特人的入侵。
statement.en:
Emperor Hadrian personally presided over the foundation ceremony of Hadrian's Wall. The wall stretched from the River Tyne in the east to the Solway Firth in the west, about 117 kilometers long. It was built of stone and turf, about 4.5 meters high and 2.5-3 meters wide, with a milecastle every Roman mile and two turrets between milecastles. A ditch about 3 meters deep was dug north of the wall. The project employed about 15,000 men from three legions and took six years to complete. Hadrian's Wall became the strongest northern barrier of the Roman Empire, effectively checking Pictish incursions.

statement.zh: 东汉和熹邓太后颁布诏令，要求各郡、国、县设立官学，招收学生教授儒家经典。邓太后认为“教化之本，在于学”，她亲自撰写《女诫》等教材，并将宫中所藏的经典抄写副本分发各郡。朝廷还规定，学生通过考试可免除徭役，优秀者可推荐为“孝廉”。此政策推动了东汉中期文化教育的普及，培养了大批儒生，但由于地方财政困难，实际执行效果有限。
statement.en:
Empress Dowager Deng (Hexi) issued a decree requiring each commandery, kingdom, and county to establish official schools to teach the Confucian classics. She believed that 'the foundation of education lies in learning.' She personally wrote textbooks such as Admonitions for Women and had copies of classics in the palace library distributed to the commanderies. The court also decreed that students passing exams could be exempted from corvée labor, and outstanding ones could be recommended as 'filial and incorrupt.' This policy promoted the spread of education in the mid-Eastern Han, cultivating many Confucian scholars, but due to local financial difficulties, implementation was limited.

statement.zh: 汉安帝刘祜为祈求边疆安宁、国运长久，下诏改年号为“永宁”。改元后大赦天下，赐民爵一级，并减免部分赋税。然而永宁并未带来安宁，鲜卑和乌桓连年侵扰边境，羌人起义虽然平息但凉州元气大伤，东汉王朝仍在内外交困中挣扎。
statement.en:
Praying for peace and stability on the frontiers and the empire's longevity, Emperor An decreed a change of era name to 'Yongning' (Eternal Peace). A general amnesty was declared, along with a one-grade elevation of commoners' rank and partial tax reductions. However, peace did not come: Xianbei and Wuhuan raided the borders year after year; though the Qiang uprising had subsided, Liangzhou remained devastated. The Eastern Han dynasty still struggled with internal and external troubles.

For Asia in 120 CE, “Emperor An of Han changes era name to Yongning” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Empress Dowager Deng dies; Emperor An of Han begins personal rule

summary.en: Empress Dowager Deng (Hexi) died of illness in Luoyang at age 41. Although she had tried hard to maintain Eastern Han rule, she failed to solve the Qiang rebellion, fiscal problems, and the cycle of eunuch-consort domination. statement.zh: 东汉和熹邓太后病逝于洛阳，享年41岁。邓太后临朝称制十余年，虽然全力维持东汉统治，但未能解决羌乱、财政和宦官外戚问题。她去世后，汉安帝刘祜正式亲政，立即清算邓氏外戚势力，邓骘等被免官，邓太后亲属多人被处死。东汉政权从外戚专权转向宦官和外戚交替专权。
statement.en:
Empress Dowager Deng (Hexi) died of illness in Luoyang at age 41. Although she had tried hard to maintain Eastern Han rule, she failed to solve the Qiang rebellion, fiscal problems, and the cycle of eunuch-consort domination. After her death, Emperor An formally took personal power and immediately purged the Deng consort clan, dismissing Deng Zhi and executing many Deng relatives. The Eastern Han government shifted from consort clan rule to alternating consort and eunuch tyranny.

For Asia in 121 CE, “Empress Dowager Deng dies; Emperor An of Han begins personal rule” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Grand Commandant Yang Zhen commits suicide after remonstrating

summary.en: Grand Commandant Yang Zhen repeatedly memorialized Emperor An, impeaching eunuch Li Run, wet nurse Wang Sheng, and others for corruption and meddling in state affairs, urging the emperor to favor worthy ministers. Not only did the emperor ignore him, but he also accused Yang of slandering the court, dismissed him, and ordered him to return home. On the way, at the Xi Yang Pavil

statement.zh: 太尉杨震多次上书汉安帝，弹劾宦官李闰、乳母王圣等人贪赃枉法、干预朝政，要求皇帝亲贤臣、远小人。安帝不仅不听，反而认为杨震诽谤朝廷，下诏将其罢免并遣返故里。杨震行至洛阳城西的夕阳亭，悲愤地对门客说：“死者士之常分，吾蒙恩居上司，疾奸臣狡猾而不能诛，何面目复见日月！”饮鸩自杀。杨震之死激起士大夫公愤，后人称其为“关西孔子”。
statement.en:
Grand Commandant Yang Zhen repeatedly memorialized Emperor An, impeaching eunuch Li Run, wet nurse Wang Sheng, and others for corruption and meddling in state affairs, urging the emperor to favor worthy ministers. Not only did the emperor ignore him, but he also accused Yang of slandering the court, dismissed him, and ordered him to return home. On the way, at the Xi Yang Pavilion west of Luoyang, Yang said to his disciples: 'Death is the common fate of a scholar. I was fortunate to hold the highest office, yet I could not eliminate traitorous ministers. How can I face the sun and moon again?' He then took poison and died. statement.en:
After Empress Dowager Deng's death, Emperor An of Han took personal control. He resented Deng's long regency and favored the eunuch Li Run and his wet nurse Wang Sheng, who had looked after him as a child. Wang Sheng and her daughter Bo Rong, relying on the emperor's favor, sold offices and interfered in justice. Eunuch Li Run controlled the imperial guards and the drafting of edicts. The Deng consort clan was purged: Deng Zhi and six others were dismissed, and many Deng relatives executed. Power shifted from consort clan to eunuchs, and Eastern Han politics became even more corrupt.

Emperor An, accompanied by Empress Yan, toured Jingzhou and Wancheng. On the return to Luoyang, he suddenly died at Yexian (today's Ye County, Henan) at age 32. Cause of death may have been sudden illness, or some historians suspect poisoning by Empress Yan and eunuchs. After his death, Empress Yan kept the news secret, hurriedly recalled her brother Yan Xian to the capital, enthroned Liu Yi, Marquis of Beixiang, and herself served as regent.

statement.zh: 汉安帝在南巡途中病逝后，阎太后和阎显立北乡侯刘懿为帝，但刘懿不久病逝。中常侍孙程、王康等十九名宦官合谋发动宫廷政变，斩杀阎显兄弟，幽禁阎太后，迎立被废的太子刘保为帝，是为汉顺帝。孙程等因拥立之功全部被封侯，史称“十九侯”。这次政变开启了东汉宦官大规模封侯和干预皇位继承的先河，宦官势力从此成为东汉政治的重要力量。
statement.en:
After Emperor An died during a southern tour, Empress Dowager Yan and Yan Xian enthroned Liu Yi, Marquis of Beixiang, who died soon after. Nineteen eunuchs led by Sun Cheng and Wang Kang conspired and staged a palace coup, killing Yan Xian and his brothers, imprisoning Empress Dowager Yan, and welcoming the deposed prince Liu Bao as Emperor Shun of Han. All nineteen eunuchs were enfeoffed as marquises for their role, known as the 'Nineteen Marquises'. This event opened the door to large-scale enfeoffment of eunuchs and their interference in imperial succession. Eunuch power henceforth became a major political force in the Eastern Han.

statement.en:
Ban Yong led a combined Han and Western Regions force of over 20,000 to Jincheng (present-day Jimsar, Xinjiang) north of the Tian Shan, where they crushed the Northern Xiongnu's Huyan prince, killing over a thousand and capturing 10,000 of livestock. The remaining Northern Xiongnu fled west of the Altai Mountains and did not dare to return east for over a decade. Ban Yong then recovered Cheshi Later Kingdom and reestablished the Garrison Commandant (Wuji Xiaowei), stabilizing the Western Regions.

statement.zh: 汉顺帝刘保在宦官孙程等人的拥立下即位后，立即清算阎氏外戚势力。阎太后被迁往离宫软禁，阎显兄弟被处死，阎氏家族成员被流放。但掌握大权的孙程等宦官很快也开始专权跋扈，汉顺帝虽然想摆脱宦官控制，但受制于其拥立之功，只能暗中培养新的宦官与之抗衡。外戚和宦官交替专权的局面并未得到根本改变。
statement.en:
After being enthroned with the support of eunuchs like Sun Cheng, Emperor Shun purged the Yan consort clan. Empress Dowager Yan was moved to a detached palace and placed under house arrest; Yan Xian and his brothers were executed; Yan family members were exiled. However, the victorious eunuchs soon became tyrannical themselves. Although Emperor Shun wanted to free himself from eunuch control, he was indebted to them for his succession and could only secretly cultivate other eunuchs to counterbalance them. The cycle of consort and eunuch tyranny continued.

statement.zh: 罗马皇帝哈德良在台伯河西岸开始建造自己的陵墓（即今天的圣天使堡）。陵墓基座为边长约90米的正方形，上部为直径约70米的圆柱形建筑，顶部曾立有哈德良驾驶四马战车的镀金铜像。陵墓内部采用复杂的环形和螺旋形走廊结构，外部装饰着大理石和雕像。这座陵墓后来被教皇改造为防御堡垒，并通过走廊与梵蒂冈相连。
statement.en:
Emperor Hadrian began construction of his own mausoleum on the west bank of the Tiber (the Castel Sant'Angelo). The base is a square approximately 90 meters on each side, topped by a cylinder about 70 meters in diameter. Atop stood a gilded bronze statue of Hadrian in a quadriga (chariot). The interior features complex annular and spiral corridors, and the exterior was decorated with marble and statues. The mausoleum was later converted into a fortress by the popes and connected to the Vatican by a corridor.

title.en: Reconstruction of the Pantheon in Rome completed

summary.en: Emperor Hadrian rebuilt the Pantheon on the site of Agrippa's original temple from the Augustan era. The new Pantheon features the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome, 43.3 meters in diameter, equal to its height, forming a perfect spherical space. At the apex is a 9-meter-wide oculus, the only source of natural light, symbolizing the connection between gods and mortals.

title.en: Pantheon completed

summary.en: Hadrian rebuilt Agrippa's burnt Pantheon, keeping the original dedication on the portico. Its rotunda is 43.3 metres across and the concrete dome spans exactly as much as the building is high; lighter aggregates such as pumice were used towards the top and five tiers of coffers cut the weight, with a nine-metre oculus open to the sky. title.en: Hadrian issues the Perpetual Edict

summary.en: Emperor Hadrian commissioned the eminent jurist Salvius Julianus to systematically compile and codify all past praetorian edicts into a comprehensive work, the Perpetual Edict (Edictum Perpetuum). statement.zh: 罗马皇帝哈德良委托著名法学家萨尔维乌斯·尤利安努斯，将历年裁判官发布的司法敕令进行系统整理和编纂，形成《永久敕令》。这部敕令汇集了罗马法的核心内容，涉及诉讼程序、物权、契约、继承、侵权等各个领域，并明确规定此后裁判官只能依据《永久敕令》判决，不得随意创设新规则。这一法典化标志着罗马法从个案解释向系统化法典演进的重要里程碑，对后世民法体系产生了影响。

title.en: Hadrian completes the Pantheon's dome

summary.en: The Pantheon, rebuilt by Emperor Hadrian, was officially completed, its dome the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the ancient world. Engineers used a technique of progressively lighter aggregates: at the base, heavy tufa and basalt; at the top, lightweight pumice and even empty amphorae. The dome's thickness tapers from 6 meters at the base to 1.5 meters at the oculus. The

statement.zh: 罗马皇帝哈德良重建的万神殿正式竣工，其穹顶成为古代世界最大的无钢筋混凝土穹顶。工程师们采用逐层减轻的浇筑技术，底部使用厚重的凝灰岩和玄武岩碎石，顶部使用轻质的浮石和陶罐。穹顶壁厚从底部的6米逐渐减薄到顶部的1.5米。天窗（Oculus）的设计使阳光在不同时段投射到殿内不同位置，营造出神圣而变幻的光影效果。万神殿至今仍在使用，是古罗马建筑技术的巅峰之作。

title.en: The Pantheon of Rome is completed

summary.en: Rome's Pantheon was completely rebuilt by Emperor Hadrian c. 118–128 CE and is a masterpiece of ancient engineering. Its vast unreinforced concrete dome, about 43 m across, remained the world's largest for over 1,700 years; the 8.7 m oculus is the rotunda's sole natural light source, and five rings of 28 coffers lighten the vault.

statement.zh: 罗马万神殿由哈德良皇帝于约公元118—128年重建，是古代建筑杰作。其混凝土穹顶直径约43米，为史上最大的无钢筋混凝土穹顶，顶部8.7米宽的“眼”（穹顶圆孔）是室内唯一自然光源；穹顶分五环、每环28个藻井，并以自下而上逐级减轻的骨料（火山灰凝灰岩→浮石）实现近两千年不倒。
statement.en:
In 128, Rome's Pantheon was completely rebuilt by Emperor Hadrian c. 118–128 CE and is a masterpiece of ancient engineering. Its vast unreinforced concrete dome, about 43 m across, remained the world's largest for over 1,700 years; the 8.7 m oculus is the rotunda's sole natural light source, and five rings of 28 coffers lighten the vault.

For Europe in 128 CE, “The Pantheon of Rome is completed” is a traceable node of Architecture change whose significance is best read through later events.

罗马万神殿由哈德良皇帝于约公元118—128年重建，是古代建筑杰作。

Its vast unreinforced concrete dome, about 43 m across, remained the world's largest for over 1,700 years; the 8.7 m oculus is the rotunda's sole natural light source, and five rings of 28 coffers lighten the vault.

title.en: Zhang Heng drafts the seismoscope design

summary.en: After years of studying earthquakes and mechanical design, Zhang Heng, Prefect of the Grand Astrology Bureau, produced detailed drawings of a 'wind-weather seismoscope' (houfeng didong yi). statement.zh: 太史令张衡经过多年的地震观测和机械设计研究，绘制了“候风地动仪”的详细设计图。地动仪采用青铜铸造，外形如酒樽，内部中央立有一根“都柱”（惯性摆），四周设有八组杠杆机关，与外部八条铜龙相连。地震发生时，都柱倒向地震方向，触发机关使对应龙口铜丸落入蟾蜍口中，从而指示地震方位。图纸完成后，张衡开始组织工匠铸造地动仪。
statement.en:
After years of studying earthquakes and mechanical design, Zhang Heng, Prefect of the Grand Astrology Bureau, produced detailed drawings of a 'wind-weather seismoscope' (houfeng didong yi). The device was to be cast in bronze, shaped like a wine jar. Inside, a central 'pillar' (inverted pendulum) was connected to eight sets of levers and cranks, each linked to a bronze dragon holding a bronze ball. When an earthquake occurred, the pillar would fall in the direction of the tremor, triggering the lever to open the dragon's mouth, dropping the ball into a waiting toad's mouth, thus indicating the earthquake's direction. After the drawings were completed, Zhang began casting the instrument.

For Asia in 130 CE, “Zhang Heng drafts the seismoscope design” is a traceable node of Technology change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Eastern Han expands the Imperial University on a large scale

summary.en: Emperor Shun, acting on the advice of Minister Zuo Xiong, allocated funds to expand the Imperial University (Taixue) in Luoyang. statement.zh: 汉顺帝采纳尚书令左雄的建议，拨款扩建洛阳太学。工程历时两年，新建校舍二百四十栋，学堂和宿舍共一千八百五十间，可容纳学生三万人。太学教授儒家五经（诗、书、礼、易、春秋），由博士和经学大师授课。扩建后的太学成为当时世界最大的高等学府，吸引了各地士子前来求学，形成了“太学生三万”的盛况。太学生后来成为“清议”运动和党锢之祸的重要参与者。
statement.en:
Emperor Shun, acting on the advice of Minister Zuo Xiong, allocated funds to expand the Imperial University (Taixue) in Luoyang. The project took two years, adding 240 building complexes and 1,850 classrooms and dormitories, capable of accommodating 30,000 students. The university taught the Five Classics of Confucianism (Poetry, Documents, Rites, Changes, Spring and Autumn) under the instruction of academicians (boshi) and classicists. After expansion, the Taixue became the largest institution of higher learning in the world at the time, attracting scholars from all over, creating the spectacle of '30,000 Taixue students.' These students later played important roles in the 'Pure Criticism' (Qingyi) movement and the 'Disasters of Partisan Prohibitions' (Danggu).

For Asia in 131 CE, “Eastern Han expands the Imperial University on a large scale” is a traceable node of Culture change whose significance is best read through later events.

statement.zh: 张衡制造的地动仪成功测定了陇西发生的地震。当时洛阳无人感到震动，但地动仪西向的铜丸落入蟾蜍口中，数日后驿站传来陇西地震的消息，验证了仪器的精确性。朝野上下无不叹服，汉顺帝下诏褒奖张衡。地动仪成为世界上第一台能够测定地震方位的仪器，比西方同类发明早了约1700年。
statement.en:
Zhang Heng's seismoscope successfully detected an earthquake in Longxi. At the time, no one in Luoyang felt any tremor, but the seismoscope dropped a ball from the dragon facing west. Days later, a courier reported the earthquake from Longxi, confirming the instrument's accuracy. The court and public were amazed, and Emperor Shun issued an edict praising Zhang Heng. The seismoscope was the world's first instrument for measuring the direction of earthquakes, predating similar Western inventions by some 1,700 years.

The Western Qiang, led by the Zhong Qiang tribe together with the Shaodang Qiang, rebelled again, raiding Longxi and Jincheng. This defeat plunged Liangzhou back into war, alarming the Han court, which was forced to send reinforcements.

title.en: Rome repairs Hadrian's Wall

summary.en: Emperor Antoninus Pius ordered a major repair and reinforcement of Hadrian's Wall in Britain. Sections of the wall that had fallen into disrepair were rebuilt in stone, over a dozen watchtowers and forts were added, and new ditches were dug. After the repairs, the Wall's defensive capabilities were greatly enhanced, effectively checking the southward incursions of the Picts.

title.en: Severe famine strikes Eastern Han

summary.en: Heavy rains caused the Yellow River to flood in Qingzhou, Xuzhou, and Yanzhou, inundating hundreds of thousands of hectares of cropland. Emperor Shun ordered the opening of granaries for relief and allocated fiv

statement.zh: 青州、徐州、兖州等地连降暴雨，黄河泛滥，淹没数十万顷良田；与此同时，并州、凉州等地却遭遇大旱，颗粒无收。各地饥民多达百万，饿殍遍野，人相食。汉顺帝下诏开仓赈灾，并从国库拨款五百万钱购买粮食分发灾民，但杯水车薪。灾荒加剧了社会矛盾，各地农民起义此起彼伏。
statement.en:
Heavy rains caused the Yellow River to flood in Qingzhou, Xuzhou, and Yanzhou, inundating 100,000 of hectares of cropland. Meanwhile, Bingzhou and Liangzhou suffered severe drought, with no harvest. Millions of refugees faced starvation; corpses littered the roads, and cannibalism occurred. Emperor Shun ordered the opening of granaries for relief and allocated five million coins from the treasury to purchase grain, but it was insufficient. The famine exacerbated social tensions, and peasant uprisings arose everywhere.

For Asia in 140 CE, “Severe famine strikes Eastern Han” is a traceable node of Society change whose significance is best read through later events.

Zhang Gang resettled the surrendered people, selected capable officials, and brought peace to Guangling. However, Zhang Gang soon died of illness at age 36. statement.zh: 汉桓帝在宫中设立“浮屠祠”，祭祀佛陀，这是官方史籍中关于佛教在中原传播的最早明确记载。汉桓帝本人信奉黄老之术，将佛陀视为神仙之一。此举促进了佛教在社会上层和民间的传播，安息高僧安世高也在此前后到达洛阳译经。佛教自此开始在中国扎下根。
statement.en:
Emperor Huan of Han established a 'Futu Shrine' (Buddha shrine) in the palace to worship the Buddha – this is the earliest explicit official record of Buddhism spreading in the Central Plains. Emperor Huan himself followed Huang-Lao Daoism, regarding the Buddha as one of the immortals. This move promoted Buddhism's spread among the upper class and common people. Around this time, the Parthian monk An Shigao arrived in Luoyang and began translating scriptures. Buddhism thus began to take root in China.

title.en: Li Gu and Du Qiao are killed by Liang Ji

summary.en: Grand Commandant Li Gu and Du Qiao, having opposed the enthronement of Liu Zhi as emperor, were falsely accused and imprisoned by Liang Ji. In prison, Li Gu wrote a defense, and his student Wang Diao and others protested his innocence. Fearing public opinion, Liang Ji released Li Gu. But soon after, he ordered Li and Du arrested and killed, their bodies displayed on the streets

statement.zh: 太尉李固、杜乔因反对立刘志为帝，被梁冀诬陷下狱。李固在狱中上书自辩，门生王调等为老师鸣冤，梁冀害怕舆论压力将李固释放。但不久梁冀再次下令抓捕并杀害了李固和杜乔，将他们的尸体暴于洛阳城外。李固、杜乔之死激起了士大夫和太学生的公愤，反梁冀的声浪更加高涨。
statement.en:
Grand Commandant Li Gu and Du Qiao, having opposed the enthronement of Liu Zhi as emperor, were falsely accused and imprisoned by Liang Ji. In prison, Li Gu wrote a defense, and his student Wang Diao and others protested his innocence. Fearing public opinion, Liang Ji released Li Gu. But soon after, he ordered Li and Du arrested and killed, their bodies displayed on the streets. Their deaths aroused widespread indignation among scholar-officials and Taixue students, and the anti-Liang Ji movement grew louder.

For Asia in 147 CE, “Li Gu and Du Qiao are killed by Liang Ji” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Parthian monk An Shigao translates scriptures in China

summary.en: An Shigao, a Parthian prince who renounced his throne to become a monk, arrived in Luoyang to translate Buddhist scriptures. He was fluent in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Parthian, and translated over thirty Hinayana scriptures, including the Anban Shouyi Jing (Sutra on Mindfulness of Breathing) and the Yin Chi Ru Jing (Sutra on the Entering of Consciousness). He systematically intro

statement.zh: 安息（帕提亚）王子安世高弃位出家，来到东汉洛阳从事佛经翻译。他通晓汉、梵、安息等多种语言，在洛阳译出《安般守意经》《阴持入经》等三十余部小乘佛经，系统介绍了佛教禅法和基本教义。安世高的译经工作标志着佛教正式在中国进行系统化传播，他被尊为中国佛经翻译的开创者。
statement.en:
An Shigao, a Parthian prince who renounced his throne to become a monk, arrived in Luoyang to translate Buddhist scriptures. He was fluent in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Parthian, and translated over thirty Hinayana scriptures, including the Anban Shouyi Jing (Sutra on Mindfulness of Breathing) and the Yin Chi Ru Jing (Sutra on the Entering of Consciousness). He systematically introduced Buddhist meditation and basic doctrines. An Shigao's work marked the beginning of systematic Buddhist translation in China, and he is revered as the pioneer of Chinese Buddhist scripture translation.

For Asia in 148 CE, “Parthian monk An Shigao translates scriptures in China” is a traceable node of Religion change whose significance is best read through later events.

statement.en:
The Cishi (Inspector) of Jizhou, Zhu Mu, submitted a memorial to Emperor Huan impeaching Liang Ji and his cronies for corruption and oppressing the people. Zhu Mu wrote that 'Heaven has abandoned him; he cannot be restored,' urging Huan to resolve to eliminate Liang Ji. The memorial was intercepted by Liang Ji; Zhu Mu was arrested and imprisoned. Only after thousands of Taixue students led by Liu Tao gathered in protest was Zhu released.

For Asia in 152 CE, “Zhu Mu memorializes to impeach Liang Ji” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Gaul region accelerates Romanization

summary.en: During the reign of Antoninus Pius, the province of Gaul (present-day France) rapidly Romanized. Latin became the official language of administration and commerce; Roman-style cities, roads, aqueducts, and theaters spread throughout Gaul. Gallic nobles entered the Roman Senate in large numbers, and Gaul became one of the most prosperous provinces of the Roman Empire.

title.en: Emperor Huan exterminates Liang Ji

summary.en: Emperor Huan and the five eunuchs staged a coup, ordering the imperial guard to surround Liang Ji's mansion. Liang Ji and his wife Sun Shou committed suicide; hundreds of the Liang clan were executed. Liang Ji's property was confiscated, valued at over 3 billion coins, equivalent to more than a year's revenue for the Eastern Han. After killing Liang Ji, Huan enfeoffed the five

statement.zh: 汉桓帝与宦官单超等五人发动政变，率禁军包围梁冀府邸。梁冀与妻子孙寿自杀，梁氏家族数百人被处死。梁冀的家产被没收，折合钱三十余万万，相当于东汉一年多的财政收入。汉桓帝处死梁冀后，封单超等五名宦官为“五侯”，宦官开始掌权，东汉政治从外戚专权转向宦官专权。
statement.en:
Emperor Huan and the five eunuchs staged a coup, ordering the imperial guard to surround Liang Ji's mansion. Liang Ji and his wife Sun Shou committed suicide; hundreds of the Liang clan were executed. Liang Ji's property was confiscated, valued at over 3 billion coins, equivalent to more than a year's revenue for the Eastern Han. After killing Liang Ji, Huan enfeoffed the five eunuchs as the 'Five Marquises'. Eunuchs now came to power, and Eastern Han politics shifted from consort clan to eunuch domination.

For Asia in 159 CE, “Emperor Huan exterminates Liang Ji” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Antonine Plague breaks out

summary.en: Roman troops returning from Mesopotamia brought back a virulent infectious disease (probably smallpox or measles). The plague spread rapidly through Rome and the provinces. At its peak, about 2,000 people died daily in Rome. The empire's total population may have fallen by a third, military strength severely weakened, and the economy devastated. This 'Antonine Plague' was a maj

statement.zh: 从美索不达米亚远征归来的罗马军队将一种烈性传染病（可能是天花或麻疹）带回帝国。瘟疫迅速在罗马城和各行省蔓延，高峰期每天死亡约2000人。罗马帝国总人口减少了约三分之一，军队战斗力严重削弱，经济遭受重创。这场瘟疫被称为“安东尼瘟疫”，是罗马帝国由盛转衰的重要转折点。
statement.en:
Roman troops returning from Mesopotamia brought back a virulent infectious disease (probably smallpox or measles). The plague spread rapidly through Rome and the provinces. At its peak, about 2,000 people died daily in Rome. The empire's total population may have fallen by a third, military strength severely weakened, and the economy devastated. title.en: Roman envoys reach China by sea

summary.en: According to the Book of the Later Han, envoys sent by Roman Emperor Marcus Aurelius reached Rinan Commandery (present-day central Vietnam) via the Indian Ocean, then traveled to Luoyang to pay homage to Emperor Huan. statement.zh: 据《后汉书》记载，罗马皇帝马可·奥勒留派遣使者经印度洋到达日南郡（今越南中部），后前往洛阳觐见汉桓帝。使者向汉朝进献了象牙、犀角、玳瑁等特产，标志着东西方两大帝国首次官方接触。虽然使团可能是罗马商人冒充，但反映了罗马与汉朝建立直接联系的愿望。
statement.en:
According to the Book of the Later Han, envoys sent by Roman Emperor Marcus Aurelius reached Rinan Commandery (present-day central Vietnam) via the Indian Ocean, then traveled to Luoyang to pay homage to Emperor Huan. They presented exotic products such as ivory, rhino horn, and hawksbill turtles. This marks the first official contact between the two great empires. Though the envoys may have been Roman merchants posing, it reflects the desire for direct contact between Rome and Han China.

For Asia in 166 CE, “Roman envoys reach China by sea” is a traceable node of Diplomacy change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Emperor Huan of Han dies

summary.en: Emperor Huan of Han died of illness in Luoyang at age 36. Without an heir, Empress Dowager Dou and her father Dou Wu enthroned Liu Hong, Marquis of Jieduting, as Emperor Ling of Han, aged twelve. title.en: Marcus Aurelius concludes a treaty with Germanic tribes

title.en: Eunuchs wield immense power

statement.zh: 宦官曹节、王甫、张让、赵忠等十人把持朝政，汉灵帝称张让为“阿父”，赵忠为“阿母”。宦官们卖官鬻爵、勒索百姓，其家人和奴仆横行乡里，百姓怨声载道。京师流传民谣：“举秀才，不知书；举孝廉，父别居。寒素清白浊如泥，高第良将怯如鸡。”。
statement.en:
Eunuchs Cao Jie, Wang Fu, Zhang Rang, Zhao Zhong – ten in total – controlled the government. Emperor Ling called Zhang Rang 'Father' and Zhao Zhong 'Mother'. The eunuchs sold offices, extorted people, and their relatives and servants ran rampant. A folk rhyme in the capital said: 'You recommend a scholar – he doesn't know the books; you recommend a filial son – he lives apart from his dad. The pure and poor are muddy like mud; the high-ranked generals are cowardly like chicks.'

For Asia in 170 CE, “Eunuchs wield immense power” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Emperor Ling changes era name to Xiping

summary.en: Emperor Ling changed the era name to 'Xiping' (Great Peace), and declared a general amnesty. But the change did not reverse the Eastern Han's decline; eunuch tyranny, peasant uprisings, and border incursions remained severe.

statement.zh:
汉灵帝刘宏下诏改年号为“熹平”，大赦天下。但改元并未改变东汉的颓势，宦官专权、农民起义、边境侵扰等问题依然严重。改元以祥瑞与赦令宣示新政，诏书所及只是名号与恩典；朝政仍由宦官把持，地方负担不减。象征性的更新掩盖不了危机。

把「汉灵帝改元熹平」放回公元172年的东汉，可以看到政治变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Earthquake in Luoyang

summary.en: A strong earthquake struck the capital Luoyang, collapsing countless palaces, offices, and homes, killing or injuring hundreds. title.en: Xiping Stone Classics are erected

summary.en: Cai Yong and others petitioned Emperor Ling to engrave the Confucian classics on stone tablets and set them up outside the Taixue (Imperial University) as the standard versions. The project carved seven classics (Book of Changes, Book of Documents, Book of Songs, Book of Rites, Spring and Autumn Annals, Gongyang Commentary, and Analects). It took eight years, producing 46 stone

statement.zh: 蔡邕等人奏请汉灵帝，将儒家经典刻于石碑，立于太学门外，作为标准版本。石经共刻《周易》《尚书》《诗经》《仪礼》《春秋》《公羊传》《论语》七经，历时八年完成，共四十六碑，每碑高一丈许。熹平石经是中国历史上最早的官定儒家经本，对规范经典文本、促进儒学传播起到了重要作用。
statement.en:
Cai Yong and others petitioned Emperor Ling to engrave the Confucian classics on stone tablets and set them up outside the Taixue (Imperial University) as the standard versions. The project carved seven classics (Book of Changes, Book of Documents, Book of Songs, Book of Rites, Spring and Autumn Annals, Gongyang Commentary, and Analects). It took eight years, producing 46 stone tablets, each about one zhang high. The Xiping Stone Classics are the earliest officially established Confucian canonical text in Chinese history, playing an important role in standardizing classics and promoting Confucian learning.

For Asia in 175 CE, “Xiping Stone Classics are erected” is a traceable node of Culture change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Marcus Aurelius dies; Commodus succeeds

summary.en: Emperor Marcus Aurelius died of illness on the Germanic front at age 59. His son Commodus succeeded. Commodus immediately abandoned his father's philosophical spirit and military policies, made peace with the Germanic tribes, and quickly returned to Rome. statement.en:
Zhang Jiao from Julu, calling himself 'Great Worthy Master' (Daxian Liangshi), founded the Way of Supreme Peace (Taiping Dao). He used talismanic water and incantations to heal the sick, and recruited many disciples. Over ten years, his followers reached 100,000, spread across eight provinces: Qing, Xu, You, Ji, Jing, Yang, Yan, and Yu. Zhang Jiao proclaimed the slogan: 'The azure sky is dead; the yellow sky will rise; in the year jiazi, the world will be blessed.' He secretly prepared for an uprising.

title.en: Cao Cao appointed Chancellor of Jinan

summary.en: Cao Cao was appointed Chancellor of Jinan by Emperor Ling. He vigorously reformed the administration, dismissing eight corrupt county magistrates and banning improper sacrifices, bringing order to Jinan. However, because he offended local strongmen and eunuchs, Cao Cao was soon transferred.

statement.en: In the late Eastern Han, provincial governors shared power with great clans; Cao's campaign tried to push central appointment back down to county level.

title.en: Eastern Han changes provincial inspectors (Cishi) to governors (Zhou Mu)

summary.en: To suppress the numerous uprisings, Emperor Ling, following Liu Yan's advice, changed the position of provincial inspector (Cishi) to governor (Zhou Mu), giving them full military, fiscal, and civil authority over their provinces. statement.zh: 为镇压各地起义，汉灵帝采纳刘焉建议，改州刺史为州牧，授予地方军政大权。州牧掌握一州之兵、刑、财、民，权力极大。这一改革虽暂时增强了镇压起义的能力，但也导致地方割据势力坐大，东汉中央政权名存实亡。
statement.en:
To suppress the numerous uprisings, Emperor Ling, following Liu Yan's advice, changed the position of provincial inspector (Cishi) to governor (Zhou Mu), giving them full military, fiscal, and civil authority over their provinces. This reform temporarily strengthened the suppression of uprisings, but led to the growth of regional warlords, rendering the central government powerless in name only.

title.en: Emperor Ling of Han dies; Emperor Shao succeeds

summary.en: Emperor Ling of Han died of illness in Luoyang at age 34. Grand General He Jin enthroned Crown Prince Liu Bian as Emperor Shao of Han. Empress Dowager He served as regent, and He Jin took full control. Eunuch Jian Shuo attempted to change the succession but was killed by He Jin.

title.en: Rome enters the Crisis of the Third Century

summary.en: After Commodus's death, the Roman Empire fell into civil war. Within a single year, five men claimed the throne (Pertinax, Julianus, Niger, Albinus, Severus), known as the 'Year of the Five Emperors'. This marked the beginning of the Third Century Crisis, a fifty-year period of military anarchy.

statement.zh: 康茂德死后，罗马帝国陷入内战，一年内有五人称帝（佩蒂纳克斯、尤利安努斯、奈哲尔、阿尔比努斯、塞维鲁），史称“五帝之年”。这是罗马帝国三世纪危机的开端，此后帝国陷入长达五十年的军事无政府状态。
statement.en:
After Commodus's death, the Roman Empire fell into civil war. Within a single year, five men claimed the throne (Pertinax, Julianus, Niger, Albinus, Severus), known as the 'Year of the Five Emperors'. This marked the beginning of the Third Century Crisis, a fifty-year period of military anarchy.

For Europe in 190 CE, “Rome enters the Crisis of the Third Century” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Cao Cao incorporates Qingzhou Yellow Turbans into his forces

summary.en: Cao Cao defeated a 300,000-strong Qingzhou Yellow Turban army in Yan Province and incorporated their elite into his own forces, called the 'Qingzhou Corps'. This force became Cao Cao's foundation; he established himself in Yan Province and began his quest for control of the Central Plains.

statement.zh: 收编不是简单的“以贼为兵”：它让曹操在兖州获得独立于袁绍、公孙瓒的武力基础，也带来军纪、粮饷和忠诚问题，后来宛城之败就暴露了这支新军的脆弱。
statement.en: Absorption was not simply 'turning rebels into soldiers': it gave Cao a force independent of Yuan Shao and Gongsun Zan, but also created problems of discipline, pay and loyalty.

title.en: Wang Yun plots and kills Dong Zhuo

title.en: Cao Cao defeats remaining Yellow Turbans and occupies Yan Province

summary.en: In Yan Province, Cao Cao defeated the remaining Yellow Turbans, incorporating 300,000 surrendering troops, greatly increasing his strength. Local elites recommended Cao Cao as Governor of Yan Province. Cao Cao began to build his own base, laying the foundation for his eventual unification of the north.

statement.zh: 击败黄巾余部后，兖州地方豪强推举曹操为州牧，曹操由此从朝廷任命的东郡太守变成一州之主。
statement.en: After defeating the remaining Yellow Turbans, Cao Cao was recommended as governor of Yan Province by local elites, turning a court appointment into control of a province.

statement.en: But Yan was surrounded by rivals: Yuan Shao to the north, Tao Qian to the east, Yuan Shu to the south.

title.en: Septimius Severus becomes emperor

summary.en: The governor of Pannonia, Septimius Severus, marched on Rome, defeated the Praetorian Guard, and killed Emperor Julianus. The Senate was forced to recognize him as emperor. Severus founded the Severan dynasty, temporarily stabilizing Rome, but his reliance on the military inaugurated the age of the 'soldier-emperors'.

statement.zh: 潘诺尼亚总督塞维鲁率军进军罗马，击败近卫军，杀死皇帝尤利安努斯，元老院被迫承认其为皇帝。塞维鲁建立塞维鲁王朝，暂时稳定了罗马政局，但他依靠军队统治，开创了“士兵皇帝”的时代。
statement.en:
The governor of Pannonia, Septimius Severus, marched on Rome, defeated the Praetorian Guard, and killed Emperor Julianus. The Senate was forced to recognize him as emperor. Severus founded the Severan dynasty, temporarily stabilizing Rome, but his reliance on the military inaugurated the age of the 'soldier-emperors'.

title.en: Severe famine in Chang'an

summary.en: Due to war and natural disasters, the Chang'an region controlled by Li Jue and Guo Si suffered a severe famine. Grain prices skyrocketed, and cannibalism occurred. Emperor Xian ordered the opening of granaries, but the grain was stolen by Li Jue and Guo Si's troops, and countless people starved to death.

statement.zh:
李傕、郭汜控制的长安地区因战乱和天灾发生大饥荒，粮价暴涨，人相食。汉献帝下令开仓赈灾，但粮食被李傕、郭汜的军队抢走，百姓饿死无数。军阀控制粮源使救济形同虚设，饥荒与战乱相互放大；皇权在武力面前无力。长安的社会秩序彻底崩溃。

把「长安发生严重饥荒」放回公元193年的东汉，可以看到灾难变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Cao Cao attacks Xuzhou, commits massacres

summary.en: To avenge his father Cao Song (killed by subordinates of Tao Qian, Governor of Xuzhou), Cao Cao led an army to attack Xuzhou, slaughtering hundreds of thousands of civilians along the way. It was said that the Si River was blocked by corpses. Cao Cao's atrocities caused widespread outrage; Chen Gong, Zhang Miao, and others rebelled against Cao Cao in Yan Province, allying with

statement.zh: 曹操攻徐州，名义上是为父复仇，实际也为了夺取淮北的粮仓与兵源。
statement.en: Cao Cao attacked Xu Province ostensibly to avenge his father, but also to seize its granaries and manpower.

zh: 曹操攻徐州，名义上是为父复仇，实际也为了夺取淮北的粮仓与兵源。

statement.zh: 它带来的后果是政治上的：徐州士民拼死抵抗，陈宫、张邈趁机迎吕布入兖州，曹操后方几乎崩溃。
statement.en: The political cost was immediate: Xu resisted desperately, and Chen Gong and Zhang Miao used the absence to bring Lu Bu into Yan, nearly collapsing Cao's base.

title.en: Drought and locusts devastate the Three Auxiliaries

summary.en: The Three Auxiliaries region around Chang'an suffered years of drought; locusts darkened the sky, and crops failed entirely. People ate wild herbs and bark, even resorting to cannibalism. Emperor Xian himself ate beans boiled with vegetables. The famine reduced Chang'an's population by two-thirds.

title.en: Liu Bei aids Xuzhou and begins to make his mark

summary.en: Tao Qian, Governor of Xuzhou, was besieged by Cao Cao and sought help from Tian Kai, Inspector of Qingzhou. Tian Kai sent Liu Bei with his troops to Xuzhou. Liu Bei had only about 1,000 men and a few thousand Xianbei cavalry, but he fought bravely, earning great fame. Tao Qian gave Liu Bei 4,000 Danyang soldiers, strengthening his forces.

statement.zh: 刘备援徐州时兵力很少，却因此进入中原政治舞台。
statement.en: Liu Bei entered central politics through the relief of Xu, despite commanding very few troops.

title.en: Sun Ce emerges in Jiangdong

summary.en: Sun Ce, using the Imperial Seal his father Sun Jian had recovered as collateral, borrowed 3,000 troops from Yuan Shu, crossed the Yangtze, and defeated Liu Yao, Yan Baihu, and others, occupying Kuaiji and Wu commanderies. Sun Ce knew how to use people and maintained strict military discipline; many heroes of Jiangdong rallied to him, laying the foundation for his younger brothe

title.en: Cao Cao welcomes Emperor Xian and moves the capital to Xuchang

summary.en: Cao Cao, acting on Xun Yu's advice, led his army into Luoyang, welcomed Emperor Xian, and moved the capital to Xuchang. Cao Cao appointed himself Grand General (later ceded to Yuan Shao) and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuping, controlling the court. 'Using the emperor to command the lords' (Xie tianzi yi ling zhuhou) gave him an absolute political advantage.

statement.zh: 曹操迎献帝，不只是“挟天子”的道德姿态，更是一套行政操作：他把皇帝移到自己的根据地许昌，用朝廷名义任免官员、发诏书、招降军阀。
statement.en: Bringing the emperor to Xu was not only a moral gesture of 'holding the emperor'.

zh: 曹操迎献帝，不只是“挟天子”的道德姿态，更是一套行政操作：他把皇帝移到自己的根据地许昌，用朝廷名义任免官员、发诏书、招降军阀。
en: Bringing the emperor to Xu was not only a moral gesture of 'holding the emperor'.

statement.zh: 袁绍谋士沮授曾劝他抢先迎驾，袁绍迟疑，结果让曹操取得名分优势。
statement.en: It was an administrative operation: the court moved to Cao's base, and edicts, appointments and offers of amnesty could now be issued in the emperor's name.

zh: 袁绍谋士沮授曾劝他抢先迎驾，袁绍迟疑，结果让曹操取得名分优势。
en: It was an administrative operation: the court moved to Cao's base, and edicts, appointments and offers of amnesty could now be issued in the emperor's name.

statement.zh: 但天子也是负担：曹操必须供养宫廷、应付朝臣，还要在“奉天子”与“自专”之间维持平衡。

title.en: Cao Cao campaigns against Zhang Xiu

summary.en: Cao Cao led an army against Zhang Xiu, who surrendered. However, Cao Cao then took Zhang Xiu's aunt as a concubine. Zhang Xiu, enraged, suddenly rebelled and attacked Cao Cao's camp. Cao Cao's eldest son Cao Ang, his nephew Cao Anmin, and his general Dian Wei were killed. Cao Cao barely escaped with his life. This was a costly defeat for Cao Cao.

statement.zh: 三年后张绣再次投降，曹操接受，说明他学会了把私人恩怨让位于战略需要。
statement.en: The loss cost him an heir and his household guard, and taught him to pay more attention to personal security and the settlement of surrendered commanders.

zh: 三年后张绣再次投降，曹操接受，说明他学会了把私人恩怨让位于战略需要。

statement.en: At Wancheng, Zhang Xiu surrendered and then rebelled.

zh: 宛城之战，张绣先降后叛，曹操在混乱中失去长子曹昂、侄子曹安民和典韦，自己也为流矢所中。
en: At Wancheng, Zhang Xiu surrendered and then rebelled.

statement.en:
The famous late Eastern Han physician Hua Tuo traveled widely, skilled in surgery. He invented an anesthetic called 'mafeisan' (literally 'cannabis boiling powder'), the world's earliest general anesthetic, and could perform complex operations such as abdominal tumor removal. He also created the 'Five Animal Frolics' (Wu Qin Xi) calisthenics for health maintenance. Hua Tuo's medical skills represent the highest level of Eastern Han medicine.

summary.en: Cao Cao attacked Xuzhou; Liu Bei fled to Yuan Shao, while Guan Yu was surrounded at Xiapi and forced to surrender to Cao Cao. Cao Cao treated Guan Yu with great honor, appointing him a lieutenant general. But Guan Yu never forgot his oath to Liu Bei. After repaying Cao Cao by killing the enemy general Yan Liang (Yuan Shao's force), he left behind his official seal and salary, a

statement.zh: 曹操攻打徐州，刘备投奔袁绍，关羽被围困在下邳，被迫投降曹操。曹操待关羽甚厚，拜为偏将军。但关羽不忘旧主，在斩杀袁绍大将颜良报答曹操后，挂印封金，护送刘备的两位夫人1000里寻兄。过五关斩六将，最终与刘备、张飞重逢。关羽的忠义被后人尊为“武圣”。
statement.en:
Cao Cao attacked Xuzhou; Liu Bei fled to Yuan Shao, while Guan Yu was surrounded at Xiapi and forced to surrender to Cao Cao. Cao Cao treated Guan Yu with great honor, appointing him a lieutenant general. But Guan Yu never forgot his oath to Liu Bei. After repaying Cao Cao by killing the enemy general Yan Liang (Yuan Shao's force), he left behind his official seal and salary, and escorted the two wives of Liu Bei on a thousand-li journey to reunite with him. He passed five passes and killed six generals, finally rejoining Liu Bei and Zhang Fei. Guan Yu's loyalty and righteousness earned him the posthumous title 'Sage of War' (Wu Sheng).

title.en: Hua Tuo prepares mafeisan anesthetic

东汉名医华佗配制麻沸散，作为全身麻醉剂用于外科手术，是世界最早的麻醉药记载之一。据载以酒送服后患者失去痛觉，可行剖腹与清创；药方后来散佚，仅存名称与用法片段。它把外科手术与药物镇痛联系起来。

把「华佗创制麻沸散」放回公元200年的中国，可以看到医学变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Library of Celsus

summary.en: The Library of Celsus at Ephesus was built in the early second century AD by a provincial governor's son for his father: a richly carved two-storey facade housing over ten thousand rolls, among the grandest public libraries of the Roman East and a monument of filial piety.

title.en: Rabbi Judah HaNasi compiles the Mishnah

summary.en: The Jewish rabbi Judah HaNasi began compiling the Mishnah, the first written codification of the Oral Torah. The Mishnah, in six orders (Zera'im, Mo'ed, Nashim, Nezikin, Kodashim, Toharot), covers agriculture, festivals, marriage, civil law, Temple rituals, and purity. It became the core of the Talmud and, second only to the Torah, the most important Jewish scripture, playing a

statement.zh: 犹太拉比犹大·哈纳西开始编纂《密西拿》，这是犹太教口传律法的首次文字汇编。《密西拿》共六卷，涵盖农业、节日、婚姻、民事、圣殿、洁净等六大领域，成为《塔木德》的核心部分，是仅次于《托拉》的犹太教经典，对犹太民族在流散中保持宗教认同起到了关键作用。
statement.en:
The Jewish rabbi Judah HaNasi began compiling the Mishnah, the first written codification of the Oral Torah. The Mishnah, in six orders (Zera'im, Mo'ed, Nashim, Nezikin, Kodashim, Toharot), covers agriculture, festivals, marriage, civil law, Temple rituals, and purity. It became the core of the Talmud and, second only to the Torah, the most important Jewish scripture, playing a crucial role in preserving Jewish identity during the long diaspora.

For Asia in 200 CE, “Rabbi Judah HaNasi compiles the Mishnah” is a traceable node of Religion change whose significance is best read through later events.
